problem: Prior attacks on VLN agents (backdoors, adversarial textures, perturbations) act on visual or environmental channels and need training or gradient access. Language-level jailbreaks of MLLM-driven navigators, whose outputs become physical actions, are unexplored.
motivation: MLLM-driven VLN agents are being adopted as the decision-making brain of embodied systems. Unlike text-only LLMs, their compliance with malicious instructions can cause physical harm, privacy violations or property damage. The authors observe that embodied agents rarely trigger text-based safety filters, because harmful navigation instructions do not look overtly toxic.
key_idea: A black-box, inference-time, instruction-only jailbreak framework for MLLM navigators with three tiers (direct, jailbreak-prefixed, camouflaged-appended) that uses a 200-query malicious benchmark and diffusion-inserted objects to make the referenced entities visible.
insight: Plain malicious queries and queries appended to a benign instruction get through at very high rates (about 85-97% ASR), while explicit jailbreak prefixes are less effective (54-84%). Jailbreak prompts contain overt adversarial patterns that safety filters detect. The models follow instructions literally without judging consequences. In the size ablation, larger models are more vulnerable under the camouflaged attack in all four categories, e.g. InternVL3-8b 91.0 vs 2b 81.5, and QwenVL2.5-7b 94.3 vs 3b 79.8.
method: Threat model: black-box attacker who can only alter natural-language instructions at inference; no access to parameters or training data.

Object insertion module: picks a neighbouring viewpoint, projects it to pixel coordinates using the focal length from FoV (following Hong et al.'s obstructed-VLN setup), and inpaints the object with Stable-Diffusion-2-Inpainting using the prompt 'add a {obj} on the center of the image'.
CLIP filter with fallback: CLIP ViT-L/14 scores image-prompt alignment (threshold 25). Low-scoring cases fall back to RGBA alpha-blend compositing of background-removed Leonardo AI object images.

Malicious query benchmark: 200 handcrafted queries, 50 each in physical harm, privacy violation, property damage and misleading behavior (inspired by Asimov's laws), plus 100 jailbreak prompts of 5 types from BadRobot and 59 object images in 7 categories.
Direct attack: the navigation instruction is replaced by the malicious query.
Jailbreak-enhanced attack: a role-play/scenario jailbreak prompt is prepended to the malicious query.
Camouflaged attack: the malicious query is appended to the original benign R2R instruction.
Evaluation: MapGPT is the navigation framework. ASR and a 1-5 Harmfulness Score are judged by GPT-4o-mini on the generated thought (following Qi et al.), with a human study on 150 samples.

setting.backbone: MapGPT framework with InternVL3-8b, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, LLaVA-v1.6-Mistral-7b, GPT-4o and Gemini-2.0-Flash (all frozen); GPT-4o-mini as judge
setting.observation: panoramic/navigable-view RGB images with inpainted objects, plus MapGPT history/map text

numbers.eval_set_note: 400 trajectories over 72 scenes sampled from R2R; 200 malicious queries, each applied to two trajectories; split not stated explicitly in the paper
numbers.extra: attack success rate, not navigation performance; 400 trials per category-averaged cell
numbers.evidence: Table 1: ASR across MLLMs and harmful categories on MP3D simulator; InternVL3 A_camouflaged Avg. 91.0

numbers_note: Table 1 also reports Gemini2.0 (direct 94.8, jailbreak 77.5, camouflaged 92.5), LLaVA1.6 (94.3/83.8/88.3), InternVL3 (89.0/76.8/91.0), QwenVL2.5 (85.5/54.3/94.3) and GPT4o jailbreak 56.5. Real-world ASR: Gemini 11/15, InternVL3 15/15. No navigation SR/SPL is reported. The split is not stated; val-unseen is assumed for the R2R subset.
results: Across five MLLM navigators in MP3D, direct and camouflaged attacks average above 85% ASR, and the best cases reach 97.0% (GPT-4o, camouflaged). The jailbreak-prefix attack is weaker, at 54.3% for Qwen and 56.5% for GPT-4o. On a physical robot, InternVL3 reaches 15/15 and Gemini 2.0 reaches 11/15.
limitations: Only a single-agent MapGPT framework is evaluated; multi-agent systems with mutual checking might resist better.
ASR is judged by GPT-4o-mini on generated thoughts, not on executed trajectories; the human study is small (150 samples), and no defenses are evaluated.
Small, handcrafted query set (200) and inpainted or composited objects; the real-robot test is tiny (5 trials per cell).
compares_to: Direct attack vs jailbreak-prefix vs camouflaged attack (own variants only)
